posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Hi

I'm using BB520 plates from Colourholographic, I also use their recommended chemistry (Sensitise plates in Photoflo and a VERY small amount of TEA otherwise you'll get too much colour shift towards blue. Then Pyrogallol developer and finally EDTA bleach). See their website for full details.

Cheers

Jem

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
I have had instant success with Fuji panchromatic film and TJ1 ascorbic developer. I also tried Ultimate 08, but the transmission holograms with the Fuji are so much brighter.

With the ascorbate developer, the Fuji film seems to be much more sensitive than what is specified by the factory. The film gets dark in about 10 seconds with an exposure of 20uJ, instead of the specified 200uJ.

I received my order within one week from FujiFilm in Belgium

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Has anyone else experienced the situation where VRP-M goes black very quickly (within 10 seconds) but still requires 2-3x that dev length to get a hologram of any kind of brightness?

I was expecting VRP-M to behave similarly to PFG-01 with regard to exposure times (slightly shorter perhaps but not much) and development behavior.

It doesn't though. At least, the batch I'm using doesn't.

PFG-01 would take at least 20-25 seconds to go "dark" but not black whereas VRP-M under the same conditions goes black much quicker but still requires about the same final development time to get a decent image.

Is this what others have experienced?

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
> I have had instant success with Fuji panchromatic film and TJ1 ascorbic developer.What are you using for bleach with this developer to make transmission holos? In the past I've found regular ferric EDTA not to work well with ascorbic developer for transmission holos (great for reflection though) but maybe with this film it works?

I used EDTA bleach. Very bright transmission hologram. Brighter than my tests with Ultimate 08 transmissions. And the Fuji film is so much faster with Ascorbic TJ1 developer than the Ultimate.

**TIP:** Kris Meerloo gave me this idea. You can use Philips Amber Deco Led for safe lights. They are equipped with replacement fittings for normal halogen spot lights. The wavelength of these lights is between 585nm and 595nm I have three of them and bathe my lab in yellow light, pointed at the walls of course. I notice no fogging on the Fuji film.

Another pleasant aspect of the Fuji Film is that it can be used for all your lasers. So no experimenting required when you switch lasers.

The film is coated with gelatin on both sides. It index matches easily on 2mm glass with lamp oil. It kinda sucks it-self onto the glass plate.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
HoloM,

I've now done enough tests for myself that I can say that combining VRP-M, a 315M, JD2 developer, EDTA bleach and Ascorbate post treatment *can* work but might not be the best combination. I've got to try a few other developers and bleaches to see if I can improve on the results I've gotten.

My latest results [are over here](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=5309).

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
HoloM,

FWIW I've now been able to get quite good transmission holograms using VRP-M pre-treated with TEA (rinsed out), exposed to 65uW, developed with JD2, bleached with EDTA and post treated with 2% ascorbic acid.

For those that go for that sort of thing I've created a [Labcast of my test session this morning](http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/archives/359-Holography-Labcast.html).
